title: The Senators Backing Van Hollen for Senate Majority Leader
author: Chantelle Lee
body:
Senator Chris Van Hollen has said that he has the backing of about 15 of his colleagues in his quest to challenge Senator Chuck Schumer for Senate Majority Leader. So far, only a few of them have publicly declared their support.

The progressive Maryland lawmaker announced his intent to run for the role last week, saying that the results of the 2026 midterm elections show that “the American people called for change,” not just from President Donald Trump but also “a change for the status quo that isn’t working for people.”

“It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership,” Van Hollen said in a social media post. “This is not about any one person—it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”

It marks the first time in decades that the race for the Senate Democratic leadership will be contested.

Van Hollen’s bid for the role comes as some members of the Democratic Party have pushed for new leadership, claiming that Schumer is too open to compromise. Schumer’s supporters, though, have credited him with the party’s victories in this year’s midterms.

Schumer has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade, and has expressed confidence that he has the votes needed to secure the leadership role in the upper chamber.

Here are the senators and senators-elect who have said that they’re supporting Van Hollen.

Bernie Sanders

Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont, an Independent who caucuses with Democrats, has publicly declared that he supports Van Hollen in the contest.

“This election was about CHANGE. The Democratic Party must CHANGE. Now is the time to take on the oligarchs and fight for working families,” Sanders said in a post on X last week. “That is why I will be supporting Chris Van Hollen for Majority Leader.”

Sanders, a Democratic socialist, previously indicated that he would not support Schumer’s bid for the role.

“The time is now to deal with the need to create an economy that works for all, not just the people on top,” he said at a press conference last week. “Do I think Chuck has been leading in that direction? No.”

Jeff Merkley

Senator Jeff Merkley of Oregon said in a social media post last week that Van Hollen has his “full support for Majority Leader.” Merkley said that he has seen Van Hollen “rally support for the people against the powerful time and time again.”

“Americans are desperate to restore government by and for the people, not the privileged and powerful. We need leadership that carries that responsibility in their heart and gut. @VanHollenForMD is that leader,” Merkley said in one post.

“Politics as usual is unacceptable,” he continued in another. “The American people have given us the opportunity to deliver. Let’s seize the day and make it happen.”

Elissa Slotkin

In a video she shared on social media on Thursday, Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan spoke about how she had repeatedly stressed the importance of “a new generation of leadership” within the Democratic Party, “particularly after the election we just had earlier this month.”

“I think that message was sent loud and clear: the American public want a new generation, and they want big and bold ideas,” she said. “I’ve been clear as well that I don’t think that Senator Schumer is best positioned to be our next leader.”

She said that she was “encouraged” that others, like Van Hollen, had thrown their hat in the Senate Majority Leader race, and offered him her support.

“Because I’ve been clear that I wasn’t supporting Schumer, I will be supporting Chris Van Hollen,” she said.

But she went on to say that, no matter who becomes the next Senate Majority Leader, “it’s going to be imperative for our leaders to demonstrate how they’re going to incorporate that next generation and what big and bold ideas specifically they’re going to put forward in the first 100 days.”

Abdul El-Sayed

Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan said in a social media post last week that he “called on” Van Hollen “to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience.”

“We need both right now,” El-Sayed continued. “Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority.”

At the Atlantic Summit on Tuesday, El-Sayed said that his backing of Van Hollen was “not against Senator Schumer; it’s more about being for Senator Van Hollen.”

“He’s unique in the Senate caucus around two things he brings together. Number one, he understands how this place works,” El-Sayed said. “But he also has a willingness to take risk. And we need people who are willing to take legislative risk.”

“Most senators don’t fly down to El Salvador for proof of life for somebody like Kilmar Abrego Garcia,” he continued, referring to when Van Hollen traveled to the Central American country last year to meet with Abrego Garcia, a Maryland resident who was deported by the Trump Administration even though a federal court order shielded him from removal proceedings.

Peggy Flanagan

Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota has also backed Van Hollen, reiterating many of the sentiments her other colleagues have expressed.

“I think people are looking for fighters,” she told CNN earlier this week. “They want people who are going to take on the Trump Administration, but I think they’re also ready for new voices to be incorporated into this party.”

She went on to praise Van Hollen for his response to Abrego Garcia’s deportation.

“I’ve watched Senator Van Hollen lead with courage and conviction,” she told CNN. “I think so many people really started paying attention to Chris Van Hollen when he got on an airplane and went and visited Kilmar Abrego Garcia, who was detained and deported. And that kind of courage, that kind of bold leadership, I think is important.”

Flanagan also said that she believes that Van Hollen will be able to “”bring together the new class of members and folks who’ve been there for a while to make sure that we remember who we’re fighting for.”
